lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Renato Annunciato | Lesson 8 -- The Development Plan

listenings.text: People assume that promotion decisions are made in the room where they are announced. They are not. By the time we sit down, most of it is already decided, and it was decided in ordinary weeks, by people who watched somebody work. So here is what I actually weigh. First, has this person made anybody else better? A manager who grows nobody is a manager I cannot move, because the region falls over the day they leave. Second, do they name their own gaps before I do? That single habit tells me more than any result on a slide. And third, yes, language. I am not looking for perfect English. I am looking for whether you can hold a room that is not in your own language, because every job above this one is that room, every single week. People hear that and think it is unfair. It is not a judgement about how clever you are. It is a description of the job.

I have read something like four hundred development plans, and the ones that fail all look the same. They are honest, they are thoughtful, and they have no dates. Somebody writes that they will improve their English, or build more visibility, and in March nobody can say whether it happened. A plan without a date is a wish with better formatting. The second failure is quieter. People write plans about things they cannot control. You cannot control whether a position opens next year. You can control whether you are the obvious answer on the day it does. So write the plan about your own behaviour, not about the company calendar. And the last thing, which almost nobody does. Tell your manager what you are working on, out loud, before they ask you. Not because they will be impressed, but because the person who is going to speak about you in a committee needs sentences to use, and if you give them none, they will use somebody else's.

extra_audio.text: My aspiration is a national commercial role, within the next two or three years. I know the gap already, and it is English, which is the declared prerequisite for the position. I started a programme in August and I am studying twice a week. In October I am presenting to the global team for the first time.

paras: Renato Annunciato has led the commercial operation for the South and Southeast since 2021. His aspiration is a national commercial role within the next two to three years. He will be discussed by the talent committee for the first time in November. This plan sets out what happens between now and that meeting.

On readiness, the committee will look at commercial results, at the strength of the team, and at communication with the group. The first two are already strong. The third is the development area of this plan: proficiency in English is a declared prerequisite for any national or regional position. His line manager raised this directly, and it is not a new observation.

The actions start now. He is attending an intensive programme twice a week, and he is going to present to the global commercial team in October, which is the first exposure of this kind in his career. A mentor from the regional team has been assigned, and they are meeting monthly. A three-month secondment to the regional team is possible, but only after the committee has confirmed his readiness.

Two further points close the plan. One of his consultants is being prepared as his successor, and this work starts this quarter; the committee rarely shortlists a manager who cannot be replaced. His sponsor will be the Commercial Director in Brazil, who will speak to the plan in November. The plan will be reviewed against this timeline every quarter.
